H is fixed with H<=0, sup H=0 and ddc H>=-C omega; every positive t<=t0<1/C gives a genuine strictly omega-psh potential.
The zero endpoint is defined separately, so zero times minus infinity is never evaluated.
Each global bounded truncation is omega-psh and the mixed bounded closed products have trace mass A by telescoping and bounded Stokes.
The local identity Theta_k=omega+t ddc h_(k/t) holds throughout a fixed neighborhood of S where chi=1.
Positivity of the bounded products bounds every local degree-j trace by A/t^j; equivalence of omega with the Euclidean trace on compact charts supplies weak current compactness.
The subsequence is chosen for one fixed t and finitely many degrees; no simultaneous subsequence for an uncountable parameter set is assumed.
Weak limits R_j for 1<=j<n are positive and closed, so their coefficient measures give S zero mass by the generalized Hausdorff estimate.
S has zero Lebesgue mass, so the degree-zero smooth volume term also gives it zero mass.
The entire local top-degree support eventually lies in a fixed compact subset of U, and its common mass is M; zero extension is used only for these top-degree measures.
Weak subsequential top-degree limit rho is supported on S and has total mass M, without asserting a unique residue distribution or an unbounded BT product on S.
The finite binomial expansion of bounded products passes to local weak limits against smooth forms, giving eta(S)=t^n M exactly.
Global weak top-degree limit eta has total A by compactness of X and bounded Stokes.
On every compact subset of X minus S the truncations eventually equal the locally bounded potential, identifying eta there with its NPP measure.
The NPP measure gives the pluripolar set S zero mass; subtraction from eta(X) proves the exact mass A-Mt^n.
The strict current bound supplies uniform positive mass at least (1-Ct0)^n A; closed-background bounded equivalence identifies both singularity volumes.
The already checked positive-volume ordinary-envelope theorem preserves both volumes and supplies the normalized ordinary fixed points.
H<=0 and envelope monotonicity order the family p_s>=p_t for s<=t, including the zero endpoint.
The ordered upper-volume formula gives d(p_s,p_t)=M(t^n-s^n); symmetry supplies the absolute-value formula.
M>0 makes t to M t^n an injective isometry onto a closed real interval, proving intrinsic restricted metric completeness.
The preceding arbitrary-t proof removes all first polar currents on every modification for every family member; hence every allowed trace pseudodistance between members is zero.
All positive-parameter models have trivial all-weight ideals but strict volume deficit, so their ideal envelope is zero and they are nonideal; the zero endpoint is ideal.
For every prescribed 0<delta<A, choosing t0 so that (1-Ct0)^n A>delta places the whole interval in the required lower-volume sector.
The complete restricted interval does not assert general model completeness, simultaneous current realization, higher-degree polar invariance on modifications or closure of full P01/P17.
